description: After fz-gee.1 the lowering doors read capture_count from the recorded ClosureCallEdge, but src/compiler2/body.rs ~799-806 CallInputMode::Closure still derives the split as callee_input_len - arg_count, with callers at jobs/runtime_demand.rs ~602 and ~2180 and jobs/transport.rs ~1832 that decide WHICH semantic input a closure argument lands in. Demand and transport place argument i at input_len - arg_count + i while native and the interpreter place it at capture_count + i; the two agree only while args.len() == function_arity, which nothing states. Two callers hold &World and could ask activation_capture_count; the third, arg_demands_for_summary inside derive_executable_runtime_demand (~886), is a pure function of &Types plus RuntimeDemandFacts with no arity source, so routing two of three would leave the fifth spelling alive. Fix direction (preferred): carry capture_count on CallTargetSummary, minted by the semantic job (which has World), so demand derivation reads a settled fact; then CallInputMode::semantic_index takes the count instead of deriving it and body.rs's checked_sub is deleted. Alternative: widen six signatures (derive_executable_runtime_demand ~886, collect_entry_external_demands ~1040, collect_entry_live_demands ~1095, direct_call_arg_demands ~2083, closure_call_arg_demands ~2104, arg_demands_for_summary ~2125) from &Types to &World, which widens the per-executable demand derivation's inputs from types+facts to the whole World and is the worse cut. Signal: a unit test that the semantic index of argument 0 equals the recorded capture_count for a direct closure edge, and the corpus canon unchanged.
title: The capture/argument split of a closure call has a fifth spelling in body.rs that demand and transport still use
